literal: Military Guards, Part 3 ○ Five Capitals Militia Levies
idiomatic: Military Guards, Part 3 — Five Capitals Militia Levies

literal: Liao established five capitals: Linhuang, the old Khitan homeland;
idiomatic: The Liao founded five capitals—Linhuang in the old Khitan heartland;

literal: Liaoyang, Han-era Liaodong, the former Bohai realm;
idiomatic: Liaoyang, the Han Liaodong region and former Bohai state;

literal: Zhongjing, Han Liaoxi territory, held by the Khitan since Tang times.
idiomatic: Zhongjing in Han Liaoxi, which the Khitan had held since Tang.

literal: The three capitals' registrable ding totaled two hundred twenty-six thousand one hundred; Fan and Han rotating households were the majority.
idiomatic: Among the three capitals, registrable levies came to 226,100—mostly Fan and Han rotating households.

literal: Xijin, Datong, and other former Han lands registered eight hundred six thousand seven hundred ding.
idiomatic: Former Han districts such as Xijin and Datong listed 806,700 militia levies.

literal: Most native Khitan households were attached to palace tents and tribes; other Fan and Han household ding assigned elsewhere were not included.
idiomatic: Khitan core families mostly fell under palace tents and tribes, so other Fan and Han levies assigned elsewhere were excluded from these rolls.

literal: Taizu built the imperial capital at Linhuang Prefecture.
idiomatic: Taizu founded the imperial capital at Linhuang Prefecture.

literal: Taizong settled Jin; Jin ruler Shi Jingtang presented sixteen prefectures, then four capitals were fixed and the imperial capital was renamed Shangjing.
idiomatic: When Taizong pacified Jin, Shi Jingtang of Later Jin ceded sixteen prefectures; the court then fixed four capitals and renamed the imperial seat Shangjing.

literal: It had one hundred sixty-seven thousand two hundred ding.

idiomatic: Linhuang Prefecture — Linhuang County registered 7,000 militia levies.

literal: Zu Prefecture Prefecture: Changba County, 4,000 ding.
idiomatic: At Zu Prefecture Prefecture, Changba County counted 4,000 militia levies.

Under the court's direct retainers, Hui Prefecture listed 20,000 militia levies.

literal: Eastern Capital: originally Bohai; its territory became Nanjing Liaoyang Prefecture.
idiomatic: The Eastern Capital began as Bohai; the Liao built Nanjing Liaoyang Prefecture on that ground.

literal: It governed six counties, twenty-six armies, prefectures, and walled posts, with forty-one thousand four hundred ding.
idiomatic: It ruled six counties and twenty-six military prefectures and cities, with 41,400 levies on the rolls.

literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianxian, Taizong renamed it Eastern Capital.
idiomatic: In Tianxian year 13 Taizong redesignated it the Eastern Capital.
Liaoyang Prefecture — Liaoyang County registered 3,000 militia levies.
